author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell raises a genuinely difficult theological question: why does Christ’s human side seem to come to the forefront in the Garden of Gethsemane, and why was that suffering necessary before the cross itself?

The conversation explores the idea of God fully entering into human experience, wrestling with fear, pain and what lies ahead before choosing to go through with it anyway. That leads back to Jacob wrestling with the angel and emerging changed, with a new identity.

Russell and his guests bring plenty of humor into the discussion, but the central point stays serious: the suffering wasn’t bypassed or avoided. It was faced, endured and walked through deliberately. A thoughtful, occasionally funny reflection on one of the most intense moments in the Gospel.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to a Sydney Sweeney advert and uses it to make a broader point about how advertising works: take something primal — desire, appetite, attraction — and attach it to a product. In his view, that doesn’t just sell things; it also shapes the way people see one another.

From there, Russell widens the argument. Whether people praise or condemn the image, he suggests both sides can end up trapped in the same pointless cultural argument. The deeper problem, he says, is that modern culture keeps us obsessing over trivial distractions that do nothing to move us toward God.
